newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson signs contract in Estonia.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson signs contract in Estonia.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications company AB LM Ericsson said on Monday its Finnish unit was to continue to be the exclusive GSM system supplier to Estonia's Eesti Mobiiltelefon as well as deliver a DCS 1800 test network.
"Oy LM Ericsson AB and Eesti Moiiltelefon entered into contracts according to which Ericsson will continue as the exclusive supplier of GSM systems," Ericsson said in a statement.
The GSM contract is worth about $20 million. Currently the Estonian GSM network mainly covers the largest towns and main roads.
"The contracts consolidate our position as the world leader in telecommunication in an ever fiercer competitive situation," said Seppo Ruotsalainen, executive vice president at Ericsson in Finland.
Ericsson is also to deliver the first DCS 1800 test network to an operator in Estonia.
The construction of the DCS 1800 network will start in late 1997.
The test network will cover the centre of Tallinn and decisions to expand the network will be taken in at least a year's time.

Eesti Mobiiltelefon is one of the country's main operators, with the majority of the company held by Estonian owners but with Telecom Finland and Telia International both owning 24.5 percent share of the company's stock.
